column1: # onramp-anchors.tsv — the registered on-ramp anchor set (ADR 0024
# "cross-surface coherence is asserted positively", temperloop#1117).
# The command a newcomer should run first is named in four places that have
# no structural relationship to each other: `bin/temperloop`'s first-run
# banner, `README.md`'s quickstart, `bin/README.md`, and
# `docs/features/install-cli.md`. Nothing ties those four together, so they
# drift silently — they did (temperloop#1116). Per ADR 0024, the fix is NOT a
# tree-wide grep for the retired name (`try`, `try --demo`, adoption-sense
# `sandbox`): that gate ships with an exemption list on day one, because
# CHANGELOG.md, docs/adr/**, and Plans-archive/** name the retired command
# legitimately, as history. Instead this registry names the specific PLACES
# that must agree, and the validator (workflows/scripts/validate-onramp-
# anchors.sh) asserts what each one MUST say — never what the rest of the
# tree must not.
# TAB-separated, exactly three columns:
#   1. anchor-path   repo-relative path to the file carrying the anchor
#   2. locator       the 1-based line number the anchor sits on (as of this
#                     registry's last edit — see § Locator drift below)
#   3. value-key     a key into the small canonical-value table the
#                     validator owns (see its own header) — NOT a literal
#                     value here, so the same canonical string is never
#                     duplicated across rows that must agree
# ── Why per-anchor rows, never one global string ───────────────────────────
# The four anchors legitimately say DIFFERENT things: README.md's quickstart
# opens with the installer curl line; bin/temperloop's banner names the first
# SUBCOMMAND to run after install; bin/README.md and install-cli.md describe
# the adoption path in prose. A single "same first command" string would be
# false against its own anchors on day one. So each anchor gets exactly the
# value-key(s) that describe what IT must say, resolved from the table.
# README.md and bin/README.md write the adoption-path phrase with the Unicode
# arrow (`→`); docs/features/install-cli.md writes it with the ASCII arrow
# (`->`) — both legitimate prose, same meaning. Rather than register two
# near-duplicate canonical values (or degrade to a substring so loose it
# asserts nothing), the validator NORMALIZES `→` to `->` in the anchor's own
# text before comparing against the single ASCII canonical value. The
# canonical value itself is therefore always ASCII — see the validator's
# `canonical_value()`.
# ── Locator drift is expected maintenance, not gate fragility ─────────────
# The validator does not require the exact line; it searches a small window
# of lines around the locator (see its own WINDOW constant) so an unrelated
# edit elsewhere in the same file does not red the gate. A locator that has
# drifted OUT of that window is a real registry-maintenance signal — update
# the row — not a false positive to route around.
# ── The negative assertion is scoped to THESE rows only ────────────────────
# For every row below, the validator also asserts the SAME window contains no
# retired value (`try`, `sandbox`, whole-word matched). That check reads only
# the windows these rows name — never the rest of the file, never the rest of
# the tree. CHANGELOG.md, docs/adr/**, and Plans-archive/** are not read by
# this gate at all and may name `try`/`sandbox` freely, as history.
# ── Known, accepted weakness (ADR 0024 § Consequences) ─────────────────────
# A surface that SHOULD be an anchor but was never registered here is not
# checked, and nothing announces that. This is deliberate: the alternative
# (a tree-wide sweep) fails worse, by shipping an exemption list that becomes
# the thing people edit to make the build green. Adding a surface to the
# invariant is an explicit registry edit — there is nothing to exempt.
# Enforced by workflows/scripts/validate-onramp-anchors.sh (a KERNEL_GATES
# entry in scripts/quality-gates.sh), with its own gate-paths.tsv row.
# ── bin/temperloop — the CLI's own first-run banner ─────────────────────────
